recommendation: Keep this commit as-is. It narrowly fixes the invalid element-path reference required by the FHIR-32497 usage note while preserving the later PA-approved FHIR-25033 wording; any further change to the short display should be handled as a separate work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-32497 is a Published/Persuasive PA change request asking PractitionerRole.specialty to be role-specific rather than tautological and to add a usage note that general practitioner capabilities independent of role are represented in Practitioner.qualification.
initial_application: Git commit 3f289b0831 applied FHIR-32497 by changing the PractitionerRole.specialty definition to the requested role-specific wording and adding the requested Practitioner.qualification comment. The current source file is in build scope because source/fhir.ini lists practitionerrole as an active PractitionerRole resource owned by PA.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-25033 intentionally replaced the FHIR-32497 definition/comment with broader wording distinguishing PractitionerRole.specialty from Practitioner.qualification. PA Confluence minutes record both the FHIR-32497 vote and the later FHIR-25033 clarification vote. The later wording should be preserved, but the current comment used the non-existent path Practitioner.qualifications instead of Practitioner.qualification.
reconciliation: Changed source/practitionerrole/structuredefinition-PractitionerRole.xml so PractitionerRole.specialty references Practitioner.qualification in its comment. The approved later FHIR-25033 definition/comment structure and the existing short display were otherwise left unchanged.
source_changes: source/practitionerrole/structuredefinition-PractitionerRole.xml: corrected the PractitionerRole.specialty comment from Practitioner.qualifications to Practitioner.qualification.
